brief.headline: Neutral tape with tech wreckage; defensives and gold holding up
brief.regime_summary: SPY sits 3.9% below its 50-DMA and only 1.1% above its 200-DMA after a 5.0% one-month decline. The 1-year drawdown is 5.6% and realized vol is 20.2%, well above its recent baseline. VIX at 23.0 is 20% above its 20-DMA of 19.2, signaling elevated anxiety rather than panic. Breadth is mixed: 6 of 11 sectors remain above their 50-DMAs, with Healthcare, Staples, and Real Estate leading on 20-day momentum. Technology is the worst sector by a wide margin, down 17.1% on 20-day momentum, dragging the index. This is not a bear-market regime but it is not a buyable dip in cyclicals or tech until breadth improves and VIX reverts.

portfolio.note: Price at $530.61 is essentially flat to its 20-DMA (-0.15%) and 29% above cost basis. RSI 52, 20-day mom -0.8%: neutral drift, not deteriorating. Next earnings January 2027; no near-term catalyst to force a decision.

Down 9.0% this week and 20.1% from its 20-day high at $1,782. Price is 10.9% below the 20-DMA and 17.3% below the 100-DMA; RSI 34.7 and momentum -19.9% over 20 days. EPS estimates have actually been revised up 8.0% in 30 days with no analyst cuts, suggesting the move is sector-driven and macro, not fundamental. The position still carries a 73.8% unrealized gain from $820 cost basis. Worth deciding how much of that gain to protect given the full bear MA stack and XLK sector momentum at -17.1%.

Down 12.0% this week to $61.62, now 8.2% below the 20-DMA and already 30.0% below the $88 cost basis. RSI at 34.1 and 20-day mom at -5.3%. WTI dropped 9.9% this week to $86.88, sitting 11.1% below its 20-DMA. The energy thesis depends on oil price recovery; without it, the technical structure continues to erode.

Up 4.7% this week to $372.52, essentially at its 20-DMA (-0.07%). Gold futures up 4.1% with RSI at 51.7: momentum recovering but not yet decisive. The 62.0% unrealized gain is intact and the position is acting as a ballast in a risk-off week.

watchlist.name: Accenture plc
watchlist.thesis: ACN is up 25.6% on 20-day momentum and 43.7% above its 100-DMA, the strongest relative strength on the screen at +31.2% vs market over 20 days. It sits in Healthcare/IT services adjacent to the top two sector momentum leaders. RSI 66.3: strong but not yet extended above 70. Earnings on December 17 are the next event risk.
watchlist.levels: 20-DMA: ~$243. 20-day high: ~$271. ATR-based stop: ~$250 (~1.0 ATR below current $260.50).
watchlist.risk: Setup breaks if the market regime deteriorates further and risk-off rotation kills high-multiple growth; ACN trades at 19.2x trailing PE, 10.8% above its historical median.

watchlist.name: Airbnb Inc.
watchlist.thesis: ABNB surged 15.6% this week on 2.9x relative volume following earnings, clearing to within 1.3% of its 20-day high at $192.50. EPS estimates up 4.9% and revenue estimates up 1.5% over 30 days. PE at 35.6x is 56.5% below its historical median of 81.9x, giving fundamental room. RSI 66.2 and price 10.8% above 20-DMA: momentum is real but entry risk is elevated after a one-week gap.
watchlist.levels: 20-DMA: $171.46. 20-day high: $192.50. ATR-based stop: ~$183 (~1.0 ATR of $6.81 below current $190).
watchlist.risk: Post-earnings volume spike fades; broad consumer cyclical (XLY) sector is not a regime leader and any SPY rollover pulls high-beta names harder.

watchlist.name: Visa Inc.
watchlist.thesis: Visa has EPS estimates revised up 13.6% and revenue estimates up 11.5% over 30 days, the strongest revision profile on the screen. Price is 3.4% above its 20-DMA and 13.8% above the 100-DMA with RSI at 63.3. At $422.65 it is a defensive-growth name in a leading sector (XLF +4.4% 20-day momentum) holding up well in a risk-off tape.
watchlist.levels: 20-DMA: ~$409. 20-day high: ~$441. ATR-based stop: ~$413 (~1.0 ATR of $9.26 below current $422.65).
watchlist.risk: Consumer spending slowdown narrative could weigh on forward estimates; no trailing PE data available to anchor valuation floor.

watchlist.name: Caterpillar Inc.
watchlist.thesis: CAT is down 10.3% this week and 31.0% from its 20-day high at $810. It sits 18.3% below the 20-DMA, 32.4% below the 100-DMA, and RSI is at 21.3. Seven analyst estimate cuts vs five upgrades in 30 days. XLI sector momentum is -3.9%. There is no technical floor visible from current data and ETF flow is net-selling.
watchlist.levels: 20-DMA: $684. 20-day high: $810. ATR-based stop for shorts: ~$588 (~1.0 ATR of $29.49 above current $558.63).
watchlist.risk: RSI at 21.3 is deeply oversold; any infrastructure spending headline or earnings pre-announcement could trigger a sharp short-cover bounce.

watchlist.name: Intel Corporation
watchlist.thesis: INTC is down 14.4% this week and 45.5% from its 20-day high of $103.19. It trades 32.3% below its 20-DMA with RSI at 25.7 and annualized 20-day vol at 137%. News flow includes a reported ~30% single-session crash tied to national security headlines and government scrutiny. EPS estimates cut by 7 of 10 analysts in 30 days; no trailing PE available. The stock is in freefall, not a dip.
watchlist.levels: 20-DMA: $83.08. 20-day high: $103.19. ATR-based stop for any long attempt: ~$49.93 (~1.0 ATR of $6.35 below current $56.28).
watchlist.risk: Government stake (reported top shareholder) could create forced support or nationalization optionality, making the downside asymmetric in ways the technical model cannot price.

watchlist.name: Gilead Sciences Inc.
watchlist.thesis: GILD is up 10.4% on 20-day momentum with RSI at 60.3 and price 4.3% above the 20-DMA and 16.8% above the 100-DMA. EPS estimates revised up 145.7% over 30 days (likely a large one-time item normalization) with revenue estimates up 2.1%. Healthcare is the top sector by 20-day momentum at +8.2%. Earnings passed on October 29.
watchlist.levels: 20-DMA: ~$160. 20-day high: ~$176. ATR-based stop: ~$161.75 (~1.0 ATR of $5.14 below current $166.89).
watchlist.risk: The EPS revision magnitude suggests a one-time restatement effect rather than recurring earnings power; fading that distortion could reset estimates lower at the next review.

commodities.name: WTI Crude
commodities.note: Down 9.9% this week to $86.88, sitting 11.1% below the 20-DMA and 21.4% from its 20-day high. RSI 37.7 and 40-day mom -14.3%. This is the proximate driver of XLE's breakdown; watch $83-$84 as the next level where the 100-DMA flattens.

commodities.name: Gold
commodities.note: Up 4.1% this week to $4,133.80, now 1.4% above the 20-DMA with RSI recovering to 51.7. Bearish MA stack remains but momentum is turning; gold outperforming the market by 4.2% over 20 days is a consistent risk-off signal to watch.

commodities.name: Natural Gas
commodities.note: Up 10.0% this week to $3.142 and 6.8% above its 20-DMA with RSI at 59.7. The only commodity with positive near-term momentum; seasonal demand and mixed MA stack suggest further upside is possible but the thin-liquidity tag warrants smaller size.

commodities.name: Copper
commodities.note: Down 3.2% this week to $6.33, now 2.4% below the 20-DMA and 5.7% from its 20-day high. RSI 42.7 and 20-day mom -5.5%: copper is confirming weak global industrial demand, consistent with CAT's breakdown and XLI's underperformance.

commodities.name: Wheat
commodities.note: RSI at 22.4 is the most oversold commodity on the screen, 11.0% below the 40-DMA and 13.6% from its 20-day high. Watch for a technical bounce, but the fundamental trend (bearish MA stack, 12.4% negative 20-day momentum) gives no structural reason to step in.

risks: INTC national security news overhang: government scrutiny could widen to other semiconductor names including ASML export controls.
XLK sector momentum at -17.1% is the worst of all 11 sectors; MSFT and ASML both sit in this sector and face continued index-driven selling pressure.
WTI crude at $86.88 and 11% below its 20-DMA has not found support. A break below $82 (100-DMA zone) would extend XLE losses and pressure energy credit spreads.
VIX at 23.0 is 20% above its 20-DMA; any macro catalyst this week (CPI, Fed speakers, geopolitical) could push vol toward 27-28, compressing multiples further.
ASML is 20% off its 20-day high with EPS estimates intact, but European export control tightening on semiconductor equipment remains an open headline risk.
calendar: ABNB earnings just reported (Nov 5); post-earnings drift window open this week
ACN earnings December 17, entering pre-announcement quiet period
MSFT, ASML, CAT, INTC next earnings: January 27-28, 2027
US CPI / Fed speaker schedule: watch for vol catalyst mid-week
